source: Jackson 2022, 'Vortices and Dust Devils as Observed by the MEDA Instruments on Board the Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover', Planetary Science Journal 3, 20 (arXiv 2109.04601), Table 1; rates from Hueso et al. 2023, 'Convective Vortices and Dust Devils Detected and Characterized by Mars 2020', JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007516 (abstract)
use: When and how often a dust devil passes the astronaut. expectedPerSol for an hour is the chance-weighted number of vortices passing within MEDA's reach in that LTST hour; sum over the sol is 4.9. About one in four carries visible dust.
perSolNote: Vortices with pressure drop > 0.5 Pa, corrected for gaps in MEDA coverage, 415 sols (Hueso 2023).
peakNote: 1.5 +/- 0.2 encounters per hour at midday (Jackson 2022), about one every 40 minutes.
dustyNote: 74 of 309 vortices showed a dust signal (Jackson 2022); Hueso 2023: at least one in five, and 75% of vortices with drop > 2 Pa.
duringStorm: Dust devils were abundant during the January 2022 regional dust storm (Ls 152-156, the storm sols in dust.json) (Hueso 2023).
notes: Hourly shape: counts of the 309 encounters in sols 15-89 by LTST hour. MEDA logged most daytime hours on most sols; the scaled noon rate (1.43/h) matches the paper's 1.5 +/- 0.2.
None were seen before 08:00 or after 20:00 LTST.
